Theme

Latin word

multō

multō (+ comparative)

adverb (the ablative of the measure of difference)

much (with comparatives): much more, much better; far, much (with comparatives); fine, punish (with the ablative of the fine); by a wide margin

In this lexicon

  • a lot

    also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.48: quī multō plūs efferunt quam accēpērunt; Cic. Fam. 4.1.1: multō ante (Lewis & Short)

  • far

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. de Or. 1.11: multō pauciōrēs ōrātōrēs (Lewis & Short); Caes. BG 1.6: multō facilius atque expedītius iter (Lewis & Short); Traupman 313

  • fine

    also used · classical · Nep. Pel. 1.3: aliquem pecūniā (Lewis & Short); Traupman 195; Traupman 315

  • margin

    also used · classical · M-O s.v. vote: suffrāgiīs multō plūribus ēlectus est, he was elected by a large margin

  • Excelsīs multō facilius cāsus nocet.: the bigger they come, the harder they fall

    classical

  • Cāsus excelsī multō facilius nocet.: the bigger they come, the harder they fall

    modern

Examples

  • an imitārī agrōs fertilēs, quī multō plūs efferunt quam accēpērunt?

    or to imitate fertile fields, which give back much more than they received?Cic. Off. 1.48
